# CookTwo

> Collaborative adaptive nutrition app for couples. One dinner. Two plates. Zero arguments.

CookTwo is the app for two people who share a kitchen but don't always share the same goals. It links two profiles to one household — a shared pantry, a shared grocery list, and an AI that plans meals around what you already own *and* what each of you is trying to achieve. One recipe is cooked once and plated two ways, with calories and macros personalized per partner.

## What it does
- AI meal planning for two people with different goals (weight loss, muscle gain, maintenance)
- Shared grocery list with real-time sync (sub-100ms) and auto-categorization
- Pantry-first cooking: type what you have in natural language, AI parses and sorts it
- Adaptive plating: one recipe → two portions with different calories/macros per partner
- Respects mixed diets & allergies (vegetarian + omnivore, keto, paleo, gluten-free, etc.)
- Installable PWA, works offline, free during beta

## Core concept: One meal, two plates
CookTwo's defining idea. Two partners cook one shared recipe, then each gets a plate portioned and balanced for their own target — different calories, different macros, same pan. No second meal, no separate plans, no nightly "what's for dinner?" argument. Portions are calculated with the Mifflin-St Jeor TDEE equation against each partner's body profile and goal.

## Pricing
Free during beta, no credit card required. Pro tier is $4.99/month and unlocks higher AI meal limits and priority generation.

## Platform
Installable PWA for iOS and Android. No app store required. Real-time sync via WebSocket with offline queue. The app lives at https://cooktwo.app.
